headline: Receiving gracefully completes the gift—accepting honors the giver and opens you to abundance
universal_truth: Giving requires receiving; blocking gifts breaks the flow of generosity
fun_facts: Many people find receiving harder than giving—it feels vulnerable
Refusing gifts can hurt the giver more than accepting them costs you
Graceful receiving encourages future generosity from others
discussion_questions: How comfortable are you receiving help or gifts?
How do you receive compliments, help, or generosity?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Giving gets the praise, but receiving is equally important. Every gift needs a receiver. Blocking gifts breaks the flow. Accepting gracefully honors the giver and opens you to what life offers.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: It's tempting to refuse help, to be self-sufficient, to not need anyone. Why learn to receive?

options.text: Receiving completes generosity—refusing gifts denies the giver their joy; accepting creates connection; being unable to receive isolates you from abundance and relationship
options.response: Yes. Refusing gifts isn't humble—it's blocking. The giver wants to give; let them. Your receiving is their reward. Generosity is a circle; both giving and receiving keep it moving.
It can feel that way, but gifts freely given don't demand return; that's what makes them gifts...

q1.title: Vulnerable to Receive
q1.script: Receiving means acknowledging you don't have everything, that others can contribute. This vulnerability is real but healthy. Independence taken too far becomes isolation.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Vulnerable to Receive"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Honor the Giver
q2.script: When you receive gracefully, you honor the giver's choice to give. Refusing or minimizing their gift dishonors their generosity. A simple 'thank you' is complete acceptance.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Abundance Flows
q3.script: Blocking gifts blocks abundance. Life offers—through people, opportunities, circumstances. Learning to receive opens channels. Those who receive well tend to have more flowing toward them.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Giving requires receiving. Blocking gifts breaks the flow of generosity. Accept gracefully.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 344. Tomorrow, we'll explore noticing what's good—gratitude. Until then, practice receiving fully.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Receiving Practice - Can You Accept?
growTrack.activity: Notice when someone offers something—a compliment, help, a gift. Practice receiving fully: don't minimize, don't deflect, just say thank you. Notice how it feels to simply accept.
